newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended the week in cautious mood as traders continued to debate whether a U.S. interest rate rise next week, now widely expected, would be cause much damage at the long end of the yield curve.

The June bond future surged on Friday as traders rushed to cover short positions on the view that a pre-emptive rate hike in the U.S. would not be the beginning of an aggressive tightening cycle and the bad news had already been discounted.
However traders said the fact the French bond contract had failed to capitalise on the positive opening, struggling to break through key resistance, left many on the defensive.
"The European markets looked pretty good this morning but we failed to make new highs and people were giving up their positions before the weekend," a futures trader at a U.S. house said.
A 25 basis points rise in U.S. rates is "definitely priced in but some say there's nothing to be worried about and others are cautious," he said. "That's what kept us in a tight range."

After opening at 127.84, up 0.52, the contract climbed as high as 128.10, just below a key area of technical resistance, before drifting into the close to settle at 127.84. Further U.S. weakness left the contract at 127.70 on GLOBEX trade.
A trader at a large French bank said the session had been fairly dull, with the exception of the last forty-five minutes when traders were closing out positions taken that day.

He said there was some potential for further gains next week on the grounds that now Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan had prepared the ground for a rate rise, some investors may buy back shorts ahead of the Fed meeting next Tuesday.

The main move in the yield curve on Friday was a reversal of the recent steepening. The gap between two- and 10-year French yields narrowed four basis points. The gap between French and German 10-year yields remained steady at minus 11 basis points.
Traders said the 10-year area had benefitted from investors switching out of shorter-dated bonds, notably in the 2003 area of the curve.

The French market emerged relatively unscathed from a heavy week of supply. Besides the 25.8 billion francs of BTANs sold by the Treasury, above its initial 21-23 billion target, another 10.98 billion francs of French franc euros hit the market.

Traders said a 2.6 billion franc 2004 securitised issue, lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Merrill Lynch, had been snapped up on the grounds the 21 basis points spread over PIBOR was attractive for a triple A-rated issue.
A four-billion franc issue by Spain, however, was less well received. Syndication managers put the reluctance of investors to buy the bond down to the tight pricing.
The 2008 bond was priced at 15 basis points over equivalent OATs and traders said the fact a 2006 Spanish issue was already trading at 16 basis points over OATs left investors wary.
The franc remained stuck in a narrow range for the second day running, trading between 3.3731 and 3.3745 against the mark.
